contexts.text: Such heat is that which putrefies...
Embalmed, that the body might be preserved from putridity, AC 6505.

It became putrid () = what is infernal thence, To putrefy = infernal filth, To putrefy is here predicated of evil; and worms, of falsity; for, when good becomes evil, it is circumstanced as is flesh, or bread, when it putrefies; and the falsity from that evil is like the worm which is produced from the putridity. AC 8500.
(These riches, and uses.) putrefy like a body without a soul; and like damp soil without the light of heaven.
When filthy delights... putrefy, and become fetid like ordure, so that (the Spirits) begin to abominate these things, then they are like soil into which a faculty of good can be inseminated.
That natural and corporeal things, separated from spiritual and celestial ones, putrefy.
They are permitted to descend into worldly and corporeal things, and thus to putrefy again.
There then appeared there as it were liquefied flesh, dissolved by putrefaction.
The fish putrefies () = that scientifics... shall be devoid of all spiritual life, which takes place when they are applied to confirm falsities against the truths of the Church. AE 513:3.
As from such a commingling (of seeds), putridity, from a spiritual origin also, must come forth, it follows that adultery is an abomination.
